findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: A digital loan borrower must be given an explicit option to exit during a cooling-off period of at least one day by paying only the principal and proportionate APR, without penalty. The NBFC may retain only a reasonable one-time processing fee, disclosed upfront in the KFS.
findings.recommendation: Remove the no-cancellation rule and the 3% charge for early exit. Build a cooling-off exit of at least one day where the borrower repays principal plus proportionate APR, with at most a reasonable one-time processing fee disclosed in the KFS. Exits the day after disbursal must fall inside this window unless the credit policy sets a longer one.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: No pre-payment charges may be levied on floating rate loans for non-business purposes to individuals (existing loans under Para 33, and loans sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026 under Para 34(1)). Business-purpose floating rate loans to individuals and MSEs are also barred from charges, depending on NBFC layer and loan size. Microfinance loans cannot carry any pre-payment charge. In other cases, charges follow the approved policy and, for term loans, must be based on the amount being prepaid. No charge may be levied where pre-payment is at the NBFC's instance.
findings.recommendation: The feature does not say whether loans are floating or fixed rate, personal or business, or microfinance. Check each loan product against these prohibitions and switch off the 3% charge where it is barred. Where a charge is allowed, make sure it is covered by the Board-approved policy and is levied on the amount prepaid. Also confirm no charge applies when the NBFC initiates the pre-payment.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: The applicability of pre-payment charges must be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement, and in the KFS where one is required. Foreclosure charges appear under contingent charges in the KFS format. No undisclosed pre-payment charge may be levied.
findings.recommendation: Show the 3% foreclosure charge, and the cases where it applies, in the sanction letter, loan agreement and KFS (contingent charges, item 10(iii)) before the borrower accepts. Block any levy that was not disclosed in this way.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: Fair practice requires that loan terms and conditions be conveyed in writing, and that a copy of the loan agreement and its enclosures be given to the borrower at sanction or disbursement. Failing to do so is an unfair practice. The Reserve Bank has also flagged excessive interest and charges as a concern.
findings.recommendation: Make sure the no-cancellation term and the 3% foreclosure charge are plainly stated in the borrower's agreement copy. Review whether a full 3% charge the day after disbursal is reasonable under the fair practices code and the Board's charges policy.

Yes, NBFCs are barred from levying pre-payment charges on floating rate loans granted to individuals for non-business purposes (para 34(1), applicable to loans sanctioned on or after 1 January 2026, and para 33 for earlier loans), but the corpus contains no 3% cap, so I cannot say whether a flat 3% charge on principal complies.

Para 34(1) bars pre-payment charges on all floating rate loans for purposes other than business to individuals, and para 34(2) bars them for business-purpose loans to individuals and MSEs by NBFC-Upper Layer entities, and by NBFC-Middle Layer entities on sanctioned amounts up to ₹50 lakh. Para 34(5) lets other loans carry charges per the NBFC's approved policy, with term-loan charges based on the amount prepaid. Para 81 separately bars pre-payment charges on microfinance loans. Under para 34, a flat 3% charge would therefore be unlawful on any loan in those barred categories, and otherwise would have to be permitted by the NBFC's approved policy, disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement, and not levied where prepayment is at the NBFC's instance (para 34(7)–(8)).

structured_content.content:
34. An NBFC shall adhere to the following directions regarding levy of pre-payment
charges on loans and advances (term loans as well as demand loans) sanctioned
or renewed on or after January 1, 2026:
(1) For all floating rate loans granted for purposes other than business to
individuals, with or without co-obligant(s), an NBFC shall not levy pre-payment
charges.
(2) For all floating rate loans granted for business purpose to individuals and Micro
and Small Enterprises (MSEs), as defined in Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006, with or without co-obligant(s):
(i) an NBFC-Upper Layer shall not levy any pre-payment charges.
(ii) an NBFC-Middle Layer shall not levy any pre-payment charges on loans
with sanctioned amount/ limit up to ₹50 lakh.
(3) The Directions at paragraphs 34(1) and 34(2) above shall be applicable
irrespective of the source of funds used for pre-payment of loans, either in part
or in full, and without any minimum lock-in period.
(4) Applicability of above Directions for dual/ special rate (combination of fixed and
floating rate) loans will depend on whether the loan is on floating rate at the
time of pre-payment.
(5) In cases other than those mentioned at paragraphs 34(1) and 34(2) above, pre-
payment charges, if any, shall be as per the approved policy of the NBFC.
However, in case of term loans, pre-payment charges, if levied by the NBFC,
shall be based on the amount being prepaid. In case of cash credit/ overdraft
facilities, pre-payment charges on closure of the facility before the due date
shall be levied on an amount not exceeding the sanctioned limit.
(6) In case of cash credit/ overdraft facilities, no pre-payment charges shall be
applicable if the borrower intimates the NBFC of her / his / its intention not to
renew the facility before the period as stipulated in the loan agreement,
provided that the facility gets closed on the due date.

11. Cooling-off period
(1) The borrower shall be given an explicit option to exit a digital loan by paying
the principal and the proportionate APR without any penalty during an initial
“cooling-off period”. The cooling off period shall be determined by the NBFC in
terms of their credit policy, subject to the period so determined not being less
than one day. For borrower continuing with the loan even after cooling-off
period, pre-payment shall continue to be allowed as per Reserve Bank of India
(Non-Banking Financial Companies- Responsible Business Conduct)
Directions, 2025.
(2) An NBFC may retain a reasonable one-time processing fee, if the customer
exits the loan during the cooling-off period. This, if applicable, shall be
disclosed to the customer upfront in KFS.
